hypotheses.title: Expired certificate on auth-service
hypotheses.summary: auth-service in prod-us-central presents a certificate its callers reject: it expired at 21:00:00 UTC. Every Transport Layer Security (TLS) connection to it fails, so callers return errors. cert-manager could not renew it because the issuer refused the request.

evidence.text: 31 TLS errors involve auth-service (reported by api-gateway, auth-service): "…hentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: cu…".
Alert SSLCertificateExpired is firing for auth-service.
Certificate auth-service-mtls expired at 21:00:00 UTC (Not After).
Alert AuthServiceTLSHandshakeErrors is firing for auth-service.
Renewal has been failing (27 failed attempts): "Vault failed to sign certificate: Code: 403. Errors: permission denied".

nextChecks.why: Is the cert-manager Certificate Ready, and are renewal requests failing.

nextChecks.cmd: kubectl --context prod-us-central -n identity describe certificate auth-service-mtls
nextChecks.why: Not After, Renewal Time, failed issuance attempts and the last error.

nextChecks.cmd: cmctl status certificate auth-service-mtls -n identity --context prod-us-central
nextChecks.why: cert-manager's own summary of the certificate, its request and issuer.

nextChecks.cmd: kubectl --context prod-us-central -n identity get secret auth-service-mtls -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -enddate -issuer
nextChecks.why: The expiry date of the certificate actually being served (the Secret named in spec.secretName).

rollbacks.title: Renew certificate auth-service-mtls and restart auth-service
commands: kubectl --context prod-us-central -n identity rollout restart deployment/auth-service
caveats: cert-manager has failed to renew this certificate 27 times: "Vault failed to sign certificate: Code: 403. Errors: permission denied". Fix the issuer first (for a Vault issuer, the role or policy it signs with), or the renewal fails again.
Workloads that load the certificate only at start-up need the restart; mounted Secrets update after the kubelet sync (often a minute or more).
Rolling back a Helm release does not help: none of the pasted Helm changes touched this certificate.
prerequisites: cmctl (the cert-manager command-line tool) is installed.
The issuer vault-internal-ca can sign again.

rollbacks.title: Roll back Helm release recommendations to r17 in prod-us-central
commands: kubectl --context prod-us-central -n discovery rollout status deployment/recommendations --timeout=5m
caveats: Helm records the rollback as a new revision (r19) with the contents of r17; r18 stays in the history.

It reverts all of r18's template changes, not only the suspect one: recommendations image tag 3.4.1 → 3.5.0; env MODEL_VERSION: recs-2026-09-28 → recs-2026-10-04; env RECS_DIVERSITY_WEIGHT added (0.15) to recommendations; ConfigMap recommendations-flags popular_fallback_ttl_seconds: 300 → 600.

If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease recommendations -n discovery), or it will re-apply r18 within minutes.
prerequisites: Access to kube-context prod-us-central with rights to change namespace discovery.
Check that r17 ran without problems before r18: helm history recommendations -n discovery --kube-context prod-us-central --max 5
